claims.text: The starting material is a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix.
The proposed intervention is addition of 2 at.% Ti to the W–Cu composite.
Adding Ti will form a Ti-rich interfacial layer.
The Ti-rich interfacial layer will promote wetting between W and Cu.
The Ti-rich interfacial layer will promote bonding between W and Cu.
Improved wetting and bonding will reduce phase separation.
Improved wetting and bonding will reduce interfacial void formation.
The Ti-modified composite will have at least 15% higher thermal conductivity than the untreated W–Cu composite.
The proposed effect is applicable from 500 to 1000 K.
The proposed effect is applicable over irradiation doses from 1 to 10 dpa.
The magnitude of the thermal-conductivity improvement depends on processing and service conditions.
The magnitude of the thermal-conductivity improvement depends on the distribution and morphology of the Ti-rich interfacial layer.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 15% conductivity improvement, but the experiment declares falsification only below 10%. An improvement from 10% to less than 15% would fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.
